REQ-SCOPE-104 What changed? is implemented here as a read-only SongActivityTimeline projection over canonical ActivityLog. No second chronology or writable timeline store was created.

Known Song/material/Version/current/approval/Session/Evidence/Learning/Focus events translate to bounded artist-facing language. Version and Asset detail resolves through canonical immutable lineage; unknown future event types degrade to generic Activity recorded instead of leaking event_type/object IDs/payload JSON.

Activity schema v1 owns sequence ordering but no trustworthy wall-clock timestamp. The consumer timeline therefore shows newest canonical recorded change first and explicitly makes no wall-clock time, elapsed-time or recency claim.

Normal /song consumer reachability is integrated as one read-only What changed? card appended to the existing Song render without modifying the 75 KB ConsumerShell implementation. The extension is explicit during normal package initialization and guards installation on ConsumerShell itself so repeated calls or module reloads cannot double-wrap the renderer.

Red-team review rejected a module-local idempotence flag because reloading that module could duplicate the card. The guard was repaired to live on ConsumerShell, preserving exactly one timeline extension per process.

Authored consumer proof covers direct ConsumerShell import/bootstrap, one-card idempotence, artist-readable /song history, newest-first event order, Activity-ID/payload hiding, GET non-mutation, cross-Song isolation and quit/relaunch persistence.
